{{Short description|Russian-Israeli physicist (1931–2026)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}}
[[File:Herman Branover.jpg|right|thumb|Branover in the 1970s]]

'''Herman Branover''' ({{langx|he|ירמיהו ברנובר}}, {{langx|ru|Герман Брановер}}; 13 December 1931 – 4 May 2026) was a Soviet-Israeli physicist and Jewish educator. He is best known in the Jewish world as an author, translator, publisher and educator.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Once Forbidden, Historic Russian Translation of the Talmud Gains Steam - A monumental effort with commentaries is launched with the first three volumes |url=https://www.chabad.org/news/article_cdo/aid/3402924/jewish/Once-Forbidden-Historic-Russian-Translation-of-the-Talmud-Gains-Steam.htm |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=www.chabad.org |language=en |archive-date=3 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260603075011/https://www.chabad.org/news/article_cdo/aid/3402924/jewish/Once-Forbidden-Historic-Russian-Translation-of-the-Talmud-Gains-Steam.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Branover is known in the scientific community as a pioneer in the field of [[magnetohydrodynamics]].<ref name=Ruby>{{cite journal|last=Ruby|first=Daniel|title=Rooftop MHD: On-site electricity from low-grade heat|journal=Popular Science|date=November 1982|volume=221|issue=5|pages=64–66|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=75dRYTqixzYC&q=%22herman+branover%22&pg=PA64|accessdate=1 October 2012}}</ref> In his personal conduct, he adhered to the customs and mystical philosophy of [[Chabad]] [[Hasidism]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Chabad-Lubavitch |url=https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/36226/jewish/About-Chabad-Lubavitch.htm |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=www.chabad.org |language=en |archive-date=26 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260526133601/https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/36226/jewish/About-Chabad-Lubavitch.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Life and career==
=== Early life and education ===
{{Chabad (Rebbes and Chasidim)|Rebbes of Chabad}}
Branover was born in [[Riga]], Latvia, into an [[Atheism|atheist]] Jewish family. His father, Hertz Branover, was an agronomist who directed the Muskati experimental farm to prepare young Jews to work in agriculture in British Mandatory Palestine.<ref><nowiki>https://www.instagram.com/p/DYACdGXjHQL/</nowiki> Jewish Museum of Latvia</ref> Branover's father was accidentally killed in [[World War II]] by the withdrawing [[Red Army]], but his mother managed to escape with him and his sister to Siberia and survive.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Branover |first=Hermann |title=Return |publisher=Feldheim |isbn=0-87306-292-2 |location=Jerusalem/New York|year=1982|pages=20-26}}</ref> He earned his [[Ph.D.]] in 1953 in hydro-energetics from the  [[Leningrad Polytechnic Institute]] and completed a [[D.Sc.]] degree 1962 from the [[Moscow Aviation Institute]], specializing in magnetohydrodynamics. Concurrently, he spent a substantial part of his time in the [[National Library of Russia]] where he learned [[Hebrew]] from whatever books he could find there, until they were confiscated, [[Antisemitism in the Soviet Union|as part of the Soviet oppression of Jewish culture]]. After finishing his studies, he returned to Riga<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Branover |first=Herman |title=Return |pages=115-119}}</ref> and started working in several scientific institutions while also making inroads into the underground [[Chabad]] movement.<ref>Branover, Herman. Return. pp. 90-97.</ref> When he first applied for a permission to immigrate to Israel in 1971, he lost his academic job.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Branover |first=Herman |title=Return |pages=111}}</ref>

As a young scientist in Riga, Branover wrote philosophical essays questioning [[atheism]], [[materialism]], and [[determinism]] and seeking God.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ברנובר |first=הרמן |title=ממעמקים: דרכי אל היהדות (Hebrew) |url=https://www.nli.org.il/he/books/NNL_ALEPH990020813040205171/NLI}}</ref> During his time in the USSR after becoming associated with Chabad, he initiated and directed a great number of activities advancing Jewish education and culture; he was among the initiators of the Jewish revival movement in Soviet Russia. Being a [[Refusenik]], he underwent  frequent arrests, interrogations, and harassment by the [[KGB]]. This did not stop him from teaching [[Jewish philosophy|Jewish thought]] and [[ethics]] to many individuals and groups. In the end of 1972, Branover received an exit visa to go to Israel. Branover was the first Jew holding a Doctor of Science degree and the title of Full Professor to receive an exit visa to leave the USSR. The ransom tax for these diplomas was 31,000 rubles (~37,000 USD then).<ref name=":0" />

=== Scientific achievements ===
Upon his arrival in Israel, Branover became a professor at the [[Ben-Gurion University]]. There, in 1977, he founded the Center for Magnetohydrodynamics Studies, which included a laboratory for the research of magnetohydrodynamics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mechanical Engineering Department Center for MHD Studies Ben-Gurion University of the Negev |url=https://www-pub.iaea.org/mtcd/nf/ws2001/israel/negev.html |access-date=22 June 2026 |website=Mechanical Engineering Department Center for MHD Studies Ben-Gurion University of the Negev |archive-date=18 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080618002415/http://www-pub.iaea.org/mtcd/nf/ws2001/israel/negev.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He obtained funding for the laboratory through a chance meeting at a lecture he delivered with representatives from the [[Office of Naval Research]]. He credits the Lubavitcher Rebbe for encouraging him to accept the speaking invitation.<ref name="Interview">{{cite web |last1=Dalfin |first1=Chaim |title=An Interview With Professor Herman Branover OBM |url=https://crownheights.info/chabad-news/945686/an-interview-with-professor-herman-branover-obm/ |website=Crown Heights |date=5 May 2026 |publisher=JEP Press |access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref> 

In 1980, Branover developed a method through which electricity could be produced through the heating of liquid mercury through a magnet.<ref name="NYT">{{cite news |last1=Shipler |first1=David K. |title=Scientists Say Future Is in Solar Energy |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/03/06/business/scientists-say-future-is-in-solar-energy.html |access-date=13 May 2026 |work=New York Times |date=6 March 1981}}</ref> His innovation was that the electrical field could be produced at relatively low temperatures. In 1984 he created a working model for his innovative electrical source. His aim was to manufacture a magnetohydrodynamics power generator to produce clean energy without the use of petroleum.<ref name="JTA">{{cite news |title=Soviet Born Israeli Scientist Develops Unique Electrical Power Plant That Has No Moving Parts |url=https://www.jta.org/archive/soviet-born-israeli-scientist-develops-unique-electrical-power-plant-that-has-no-moving-parts |access-date=13 May 2026 |work=Daily News Bulletin |agency=Jewish Telegraphic Agency |date=6 April 1984 |archive-date=25 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250625083353/https://www.jta.org/archive/soviet-born-israeli-scientist-develops-unique-electrical-power-plant-that-has-no-moving-parts |url-status=live }}</ref> A research and development company, Solmecs, was created to market Branover's magnetohydrodynamics generator and many technological by-products of his research.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Branover |last2=Lesin |first1=H. |first2=S. |title=Liquid Metal Systems |date=1995 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-1-4613-5814-5 |location=Boston |pages=377-392 |language=en|chapter=Experience in Operating Heavy Liquid Metal MHD Two-PhasenFlow Systems}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Branover |first=H. |date=1993 |title=Liquid Metal MHD Research and Development in Israe; |url=https://inis.iaea.org/records/y4hhg-p3f74 |access-date=22 June 2026 |website=International Atomic Energy Agency}}</ref> He published over 300 professional papers and textbooks on the behavior of liquid metals in magenetic fields (see "Works" below).  

===Activism for Russian Jews===
In addition to his scientific achievements, Branover was an active spiritual leader of Jews in the Soviet Union and later emigrants to Israel. He chaired the Shamir Association of Professionals from the USSR and served as [[editor-in-chief]] of its [[publishing house]] which printed over 400 titles of [[Torah| Torah literature]] in Russian, notably translations of the Pentateuch with commentaries, prayer books, the Code of Jewish Law, Maimonides, Yehuda Halevi, and the ''Tanya''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SHAMIR Publishing House |url=https://www.yahad.org/38422.html?srsltid=AfmBOorXzBG7k1cCQwBuR9yUF6AahM5e0tvK2FZr37axAjl7YVquxf66 |archive-date= |access-date=2 July 2026 |website=Yachad}}</ref> Branover was also the founding editor-in-chief of the ''B'Or Ha'Torah Journal of Science, Life and Art in the Light of the Torah''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B'Or Ha'Torah (BHT) |url=https://www.jct.ac.il/en/publications/bor-hatorah/ |website=JCT Lev Academic Center}}</ref> Together with Rabbi Shalom D. Lipskar of The Shul of Bal Harbour, ''B'Or Ha'Torah'' organized 15 international conferences on Torah and science in Miami.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mission & History |url=https://www.cyscollege.org/mission-history-1 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=cyscollege |language=en}}</ref>

Under Branover's direction, SHAMIR established a well-accredited Jewish day school<ref>{{Cite web |title=School “Shamir” |url=https://school-shamir.ru/english/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=school-shamir.ru}}</ref> in [[Saint Petersburg]], Russia. Together with Rabbi Natan Barkan and Professor Ruvin Ferber, Branover organized international conferences in Riga entitled "Jews in a Changing World."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Umanovska |first=Gita |date=2017-04-19 |title=Conference JEWS IN A CHANGING WORLD |url=https://jews.lv/en/conference-jews-in-a-changing-world/news-and-events/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=Jewish Community of Latvia |language=en-US}}</ref>  

In 1987 Branover founded [[SATEC]], which started out as a technological business incubator, soon after focusing on the development and manufacturing of power metering solutions, such as power meters and power quality analyzers. This move was inspired<ref>{{Cite web|title=Laser Vision|url=https://www.chabad.org/therebbe/article_cdo/aid/4175303/jewish/Laser-Vision.htm|access-date=2020-08-11|website=www.chabad.org|language=en|archive-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204085756/https://www.chabad.org/therebbe/article_cdo/aid/4175303/jewish/Laser-Vision.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> by the [[Menachem Mendel Schneerson|Lubavitcher Rebbe]], who predicted an influx of Jewish immigration from the Soviet Union, following [[Perestroika]]. His aim was to create jobs in a fitting technological environment for these immigrants,<ref>{{Cite web|first=Eleanor |last=Shapiro |title=Immigration of Soviet Jews Causes Unease Among Israelis|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-1990-05-20-9001090249-story.html|access-date=2020-08-11|website=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=20 May 1990|language=en-US|archive-date=1 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210701215912/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-1990-05-20-9001090249-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> many of them holding advanced scientific degrees and in-depth technological experience.

In 1991, the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences invited Branover to supervise its 8-volume ''Encyclopedia of Russian Jewry''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Guide to Jewish Encyclopedias (In Russia & Eastern Europe) {{!}} Slavic, East European & Eurasian Studies {{!}} University Library {{!}} Illinois |url=https://www.library.illinois.edu/slavic/subsourgen/encyclopedias/judaicaenc/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=www.library.illinois.edu}}</ref> Covering 1000 years, the encyclopedia details the contribution of Jews to Russian and world [[civilization]]. The late [[Isaiah Berlin]] of [[Oxford]] was the first chief consultant of the encyclopedia, [[Martin Gilbert]] was its second chief consultant, and the Israeli Ministry of Education helped support the project.  

=== Personal life ===
Branover was a dedicated [[Hasid]] of [[Menachem M. Schneerson|Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson]].

Branover was married to Fania Branover who died in 2012. Their only child is Danny Branover.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Fania Branover, 75, OBM |url=https://collive.com/fania-branover-75-obm/ |archive-url= |access-date= |website= |language=}}</ref>

Herman Yirmiyahu Branover died in New York on 4 May 2026, at the age of 94, and was buried in the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-04 |title=BDE: Professor Herman Branover, 94, OBM |url=https://crownheights.info/chabad-news/945532/bde-professor-herman-branover-94-obm/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=CrownHeights.info |language=en |archive-date=5 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260505130615/https://crownheights.info/chabad-news/945532/bde-professor-herman-branover-94-obm/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Works==
*His early philosophical [[manuscript]]s were secretly reproduced and smuggled out of the [[USSR]] to [[Israel]] and published there in [[Russian language|Russian]] and [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] by the [[Israeli Ministry of Education]].<ref name="borhatorah">{{cite web|last=Branover|first=Yermiyahu (Herman)|url=http://www.borhatorah.org/home/branover/branover.html|title=B'or Ha'torah 
| url-status = dead 
| archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120224182926/http://www.borhatorah.org/home/branover/branover.html
| archivedate = 24 February 2012 
}}</ref>
*While in the USSR, Branover undertook to translate some of the fundamental [[Rabbinic literature|works of Judaism]] into Russian. He continued this work in Israel through SHAMIR, where he organized and trained a team of [[translator]]s and [[editing|editors]] to complete and expand his work, which included most importantly the [[Chumash (Judaism)|Pentateuch]] with [[Rabbinic literature#Meforshim|commentaries]], the [[Shlomo Ganzfried#Kitzur Shulchan Aruch|Code of Jewish Law]], and writings of [[Maimonides]] and [[Yehuda Halevy]]. Over 12 million copies of 400 titles of Russian-language Judaica were published by SHAMIR.<ref name="borhatorah" /> 
*Branover's autobiography Return, including ''De Profundis'', a collection of his early philosophical essays has been published in Russian, [[Spanish language|Spanish]], [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]], [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] and English.<ref name="borhatorah" />
*Branover founded the periodical ''B’Or Ha’Torah'' in 1981 at the urging of the late Lubavitcher Rebbe, [[Menachem Mendel Schneerson]], who gave the periodical its name.  The publication allowed distinguished scientists – initially those close to the Rebbe –  to bring their discussions of apparent contradictions between Torah and science to a wider audience. Out of 97 authors, 28 were Chabad Hasidim and 69 were not. Most of the [[peer review|referees]] were not affiliated with Chabad.
'''Herman Branover's published science and technology works include:'''

*''MHD bluff body turbulent wake stabilization'' (2003)<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Magnetohydrodynamics|date=2003|title=MHD bluff body turbulent wake stabilization}}</ref>
*''Single- and Multi-Phase Flows in an Electromagnetic Field: Energy, Metallurgical, and Solar Applications'' <ref>{{cite book |title=Single- and Multi-Phase Flows in an Electromagnetic Field: Energy, Metallurgical, and Solar Applications |date=1 January 1985 |publisher=American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics |isbn=978-0-930403-04-1 |url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/book/10.2514/4.865688 |language=en}}</ref>
*''Magnetohydrodynamic Flow in Ducts'' (Wiley/Israel Universities Press, 1978)
*"Turbulence and Structures: Chaos, Fluctuations, and Helical Self-organization" in ''Nature and the Laboratory'' (Academic Press, 1999).
*"The Growth of Magnetohydrodynamics in Latvia and Israel: A retrospective on the evolution of MHD technology" (Springer, 2007).
*"Liquid-Metal Flows and Magnetohydrodynamics: Proceedings from the 3rd Beer-Sheva International Seminar" (AIAA, 1983).
*"Experimental investigation of the origin of residual disturbances in turbulent MHD flows after laminarization" ''Journal of Fluid Mechanics'' (1979).
*Branover, H. & Chkhetiani, O. & Eidelman, Alexander & Golbraikh, E. & Moiseev, S. (2001). "Chiral phenomena in MHD and MHD-like media." ''Magnetohydrodynamics'' '''37''', 06-01-2001.
*"The Growth of Magnetohydrodynamics in Latvia and Israel": A retrospective on the evolution of MHD technology (Springer, 2007).
*Branover H.H. and Lielausis O., "The characteristics of the transverse magnetic field effect onturbulent flow of liquid metal at different Reynolds numbers." ''Sov. Phys.-Techn. Phys''. '''10''' (1965) 191–195.
